title: EMA qualifies AIM-NASH after AI-assisted pathologists scored MASH liver biopsies more accurately than pathologists reading alone
summary: EMA qualified PathAI's AIM-NASH after a 1,481-case validation in which AI-assisted pathologists agreed better with expert panels on inflammation and ballooning.
account: PathAI of Boston built AIM-NASH, a set of deep learning models that score liver biopsy slides for the features that define metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) in drug trials. A pathologist reviews each AI score and accepts or rejects it. In the clinical validation that PathAI submitted to the European Medicines Agency (EMA) in June 2023, 1,481 biopsy cases from four completed trials of obeticholic acid, pegbelfermin and semaglutide were scored by panels of two expert liver pathologists with a third as tiebreaker, by individual pathologists reading alone, and by pathologists using the tool. Agreement with the panel, measured by weighted kappa, was higher with the tool for lobular inflammation (0.419 against 0.297) and hepatocellular ballooning (0.563 against 0.414), and similar for steatosis and fibrosis. EMA's human medicines committee (CHMP) endorsed this conclusion and adopted its first qualification opinion for an AI-based method on 27 February 2025, which means that the committee can accept evidence from the tool in future applications. The committee noted open questions on the clinical meaning of the gains, and the qualification covers only the locked version of the tool with one scanner model. PathAI and four drug companies funded the study, and several authors were PathAI employees.
purpose: AIM-NASH was built to help trial pathologists score MASH biopsies with less variability. More accurate and consistent scoring is that purpose.
system: AIM-NASH (Artificial Intelligence-Based Measurement of NASH histology; also called AIM-MASH)
deployer: PathAI with sponsors of MASH drug trials (validation on archived biopsies from trials of obeticholic acid, pegbelfermin and semaglutide)
location: Multinational MASH clinical trials (central pathology reading)

ratings.reason: Weighted kappa against the expert panel rose from 0.297 to 0.419 for lobular inflammation and from 0.414 to 0.563 for ballooning in 1,481 cases.

ai_role.statement: The validation compared AI-assisted reads with unassisted individual pathologist reads of the same 1,481 cases against the same expert panel.

evidence.title: Qualification opinion for Artificial Intelligence-Based Measurement of Non-alcoholic Steatohepatitis Histology in Liver Biopsies to Determine Disease Activity in NASH/MASH Clinical Trials
evidence.quote: The Applicant concludes that the accuracy analysis demonstrated that the AI-assisted scores were superior to the manual pathologist scoring for lobular inflammation and hepatocellular ballooning and non-inferior for steatosis and fibrosis. Secondary and exploratory analysis also demonstrated improved accuracy of the AI-assisted scoring compared to manual pathologist evaluation. This overall conclusion is endorsed, but some questions on clinical meaningfulness on comparison to literature reports remain.
